'''Faustina Pignatelli Carafa''', princess of Colubrano (9 December 1705 – 30 December 1769),<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.treccani.it//enciclopedia/faustina-pignatelli_(Dizionario-Biografico)|title=PIGNATELLI, Faustina in "Dizionario Biografico"|website=www.treccani.it|language=it-IT|access-date=2019-11-20}}</ref> was an Italian mathematician and scientist from Naples. She became the second woman (after the Bolognese physicist [[Laura Bassi]])<ref name=":0" /> to be elected to the [[Academy of Sciences of Bologna]] on 20 November 1732.<ref>Ancient Archives of the Accademia delle Scienze dell'Istituto di Bologna. Atti, fasc. 5.</ref>

In 1734, Faustina published a paper titled ''Problemata Mathematica'' using the name "anonima napolitana" (a Latin phrase meaning "anonymous female from Naples"), in the German scientific journal ''[[Nova Acta Eruditorum]]'', which was published entirely in Latin.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://scienzaa2voci.unibo.it/biografie/84-pignatelli-carafa-faustina-principessa-di|title=Pignatelli, Carafa Faustina, principessa di Colubrano — Scienza a due voci|website=scienzaa2voci.unibo.it|access-date=2019-11-20}}</ref>

Alongside her brother Peter, she was educated by [[Nicola De Martino]] and was instrumental in introducing the theories of [[Isaac Newton]] to Naples. She was an important participator in the scientific debate in Italy and corresponded with the French Academy of Sciences.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last=Bertucci|first=Paola|date=2013|title=The In/visible Woman: Mariangela Ardinghelli and the Circulation of Knowledge between Paris and Naples in the Eighteenth Century|journal=Isis|language=en|volume=104|issue=2|pages=226–249|doi=10.1086/670946|pmid=23961687|s2cid=6638864}}</ref>

Upon her marriage to the poet Francesco Domenico [[House of Carafa|Carafa]] in 1724, she was given the principality Colubrano in southern Italy as a dowry by her father.<ref name=":0" />

[[Francesco Maria Zanotti]], secretary of the [[Academy of Sciences of the Institute of Bologna|Academy of Sciences of Bologna]] from 1723 to 1766, mentioned her as a gifted mathematician in 1745.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" />

She was a Dame of the [[Order of the Starry Cross]] from 3 May 1732.<ref>{{Cite book|title=La radunanza nobile, e pia della crociera fondata dalla sacra cesarea real maestà dell'imperatrice Eleonora per clementissimo comando della S.C.R.M.A|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QcZTAAAAcAAJ|year=1761|editor=appresso Gio. Tomaso Trattner, stampatore di corte|place=In Vienna|language=it|page=56}}</ref>
